PRICING SELECTION allows a shorthand method of setting the pricing functions. If a number from one to nine is entered into the PRICING SELECTION function, a corresponding standard setting (shown in bold type above) will be entered into the game. The rest of the pricing functions are automatically set for that standard.

THE PRICE OF ONE GAME (number of coins per game) is equal to the number of SLOT UNITS for any one slot divided by the number of UNITS PER CREDIT. If the number of LEFT SLOT UNITS (or RIGHT SLOT UNITS) equals X and the number of UNITS PER CREDIT equals Y, then the price of one game Is X/V.
UNITS REQUIRED FOR BONUS CREDIT is the number of games that must be purchased before a free game is awarded.

MINIMUM UNITS FOR ANY CREDIT is the least number of coins allowed per game or games: Or. put another way, the MINIMUM UNITS FOR ANY CREDIT determines the smallest number of whole games that may be paid for at one time. C1 CHECK ON-BOARD POWER SUPPLY
(1) With power off, test for fuse continuity at F4 and F2.
(2) With power on, check for +42V unregulated DC at TP4 and at pin 5 of IC4.
(3) Now check for +5V regulated DC between TP4 and TP3. If voltages are absent or low, turn off game and lift one pin of filter capacitors C25, C26 and C27.
(4) Check each with ohmmeter for possible shorts.
(5) If capacitors are good and unregulated voltages test okay but you're missing +5V, replace regulator chip (IC8). C CHECK AUDIO (ANALOG) SECTION

(4) Turn power on; turn up volume control. Momentarily place powered-up AC soldering pencil on final amplifier's input pin (IC4, pin 1 or 10P4, pin 2). If you hear low hum, audio IC, volume pot and speaker are okay.

(2) Repeat test at Q2 emitter. If you hear hum, analog section is okay. Step (1) will also work if you simply touch amplifier’s input pin. However oufput level of hum will be much lower than with soldering iron. DO NOT use a soldering pencil of over 40 watts. Cordless models will NOT work here.
